_about: PARKED. What each face button holds in each stance. The martial arts stance follows docs/design/brawl-second-pass.md (three strengths: X light, Y medium, B heavy; A the body; the signature on RT + B). The other stances follow docs/design/melee-press-feel.md sections 10, 11 and 13 until their slices. A filter is part values that must all hold; any is a list of filters of which one must. presses holds what one press of a button asks for when it is not a form of the button's own pool. needs lists what a cell asks of others before it can play
_spread: each pick marks down the shapes that share its path, its target or its tip, and more those that share limb, path and target, so a cell spreads over the grammar

x.what: light strikes: the light (tapped), the flurry blow (mashed), the burst (held), the skill strike and the juggle strike (on the beat)
x._quotas: filled in this order before the cell is filled freely. The first five are the stick's leans (a weight of 3 at run time, not a filter). The last two keep both readings deep: a juggle is up to 5 skill strikes (Orb)

hold.what: the burst: eight lights on a held X, slowing on a curve. One string for each lean of the stick; the director plays one whole when its first blow is the light the press threw, or composes one by the same rules (parts.json strike.burst)

needs.what: the burst at its gaps: the first three blows land 4, 4 and 5 ticks apart, inside the 5 ticks of the carry between blows
the burst as a move of eight; the pick of each blow by its gap's class
one breath of sound for the eight

share._about: his own lights, at least, by his tier (Game Design: 3 at tier 1, 5 at tier 2). A light that is one fighter's own is never lent, so there is no cap to keep: maxWithOne is the whole cell

x._ownFlurry: Combat's, for Game Design's gate: three of his own lights fit the flurry's gap (the whole of a tier-1 floor), since two blows in three of a match are flurry blows and a fighter whose own lights are all kicks would be seen throwing nobody's hands

y.what: medium strikes, which were the heavy strikes: the medium (tapped), the medium flurry (mashed), the charged medium (held), the medium skill strike (on the beat)

quotas.name: the stop: quick, on a line or a rise
the grind: quick, a drop or an arc

y._quotas: the first four are how the cell was filled when these were the heavies, by where each sends; a medium no longer knocks back. quick is the count that read on a 12-tick wind-up: the rest are thrown on a held Y only

share._about: his own mediums, at least, by his tier (Game Design: 2 at tier 1, 3 at tier 2). Never lent, as his lights are

y._quotasSplit: The split by path (docs/combat/nine-cells-look.md; the EP's go of 2026-10-15): each style of the button draws on its own pieces, so each group keeps 5, one above the picker's least (never one of his last two). Y: tapped, the stop (a quick medium on a line or a rise); mashed, the grind (a drop or an arc); held, the mediums with a long wind-up. B: tapped, all of them; mashed, the advance (a line or a drop); held, the big read (an arc, a rise or a spin). A fighter whose locked moves fall short gets a place added in his row (identity `adds`), and the quota fills it

held: his channel (On the Chin for the rival)

needs.what: contextHeld; the aimed throw as a knock-back; the grab lockout of 90 ticks
a second look for each grab and throw (wave 4's grabs: designed, not posed)

clinch.what: the vicious blows inside the clinch (docs/combat/grapple-hybrid.md): X, Y and B are close blows on the region the stick leans to; one arm may be on the grip, so a hand blow is one hand
clinch._quotas: The four regions of the vicious map (parts.json vicious.regions: up the head, toward the core, down the legs, away the arms), so a held stick always has a blow; the core most, since it is the no-stick region. Two of his own at least, as for any cell with a share rule
clinch._anyWeight: A vicious blow has one worth whatever its look (half a brawl light, three times its wear: brawl-second-pass.md section 4), so a shape is one place: the better-covered of its light and medium key sets
clinch._share: Game Design's floors of a fighter's own are ruled for X, Y and B (fighter-pipeline.md section 1). The clinch is new: a tier-1 newcomer may start on the common vicious blows, as he may borrow heavies, and a fighter who ships at tier 2 has two of his own. The two in the build have five each

never.why: in a hold a foot goes low only: a sweep or a low kick to the legs or the shins

clinch._places: Legal's s08 counts by place, and Game Design re-ruled the clinch that way (grapple.md section 2): no more than two in a row to one place, so a region held on the stick alternates places. So each place of the head, the core and the legs has a piece (the shins only a foot on an arc in reaches, so the clinch takes a foot, low only). The arm is one target in the grammar; its places (shoulder, elbow, wrist) are assigned by Animation at run time (Legal's launcher-and-reach-screen)

b.what: heavy strikes, a new tier of whole-body blows: the heavy (tapped), the heavy flurry (mashed), the charged heavy with its knock-back, launch or lift (held), the heavy skill strike (on the beat)
b._notLevels: the tier is new looks: a shape that one of his posed pieces can stand in for is not one of the ten. It is in the stand-in cell
b._spread: each heavy is seen whole, so the same limb, tip and path at another place is marked down hard: no two of the ten are one blow aimed twice

standIn._without: posed strikes left out of a fighter's stand-ins. The Protagonist's spinning heel lands on the chest, as three of his others do, and it is a spin, as two are: with it, a mashed B could reach a point where no stand-in may follow under Legal's string rules. Without it his five never run dry (the EP's ruling)
standIn.what: the fallback for B: his posed mediums that only read on a long wind-up, played at B's wind-up when no heavy of the tier may be thrown. They stood in for the whole tier until Animation posed its first eight a fighter. Not locked

quotas.name: the advance: a line or a drop
the big read: an arc, a rise or a spin

b._quotas: a launcher for each way the stick can send him first (the check holds every tier to it, and a fighter who borrows under the share rule would else end without one); then two for each way a charged heavy can send the rival (the two that send up are also the lift), then two for each lean of the stick, so a flurry of four held on one lean still shows four blows

needs.what: every heavy that is waiting: a wind-up held in plain sight, the blow and its end; and the stand-ins played at 28 ticks
B as a strike button: the 28-tick wind-up and its armour, the flurry, the pick by lean and by links
the tier seen drawn: each drive's tell, and each heavy (condition W1)
how the ground answers a heavy that lands

share._about: Game Design's rule for a shared heavy tier (docs/design/fighter-pipeline.md section 1). own: how many of the cell's pieces are his alone, by his tier (identity.json `tier`, 1 when it is not said): of a pack of his own, or a new shape that no other fighter's cell holds. maxWithOne: the most of the cell he may share with any one other fighter, as a part of its count. The fighter he takes a piece from keeps his own share as well. A pack he lists under `borrows` is another fighter's. Fighters with the same `alt` are options for one place in the roster and never count each other

b._quotasSplit: The split by path (docs/combat/nine-cells-look.md; the EP's go of 2026-10-15): each style of the button draws on its own pieces, so each group keeps 5, one above the picker's least (never one of his last two). Y: tapped, the stop (a quick medium on a line or a rise); mashed, the grind (a drop or an arc); held, the mediums with a long wind-up. B: tapped, all of them; mashed, the advance (a line or a drop); held, the big read (an arc, a rise or a spin). A fighter whose locked moves fall short gets a place added in his row (identity `adds`), and the quota fills it

reach._distinct: Legal's e06 counts a piece by its hand state, release and body, so two bolts of one hand and release are one piece to it, whatever place they are set on. The four differ in hand or release, so that a mash always has one it may throw
reach.what: the point-blank bolt: with RB held in reach, a bolt fired with the hand on him. It takes a light's place in a string; mashed, the piece changes every blow

RB held in reach: X as a light that is a shot; the pick that never throws the same piece twice running
a crack for the shot against the thud of a fist

the order of a mashed run by the rules of reach.run, with the arm for each bolt

gate._about: Game Design's gate on blows (fighter-pipeline.md section 1): at least a quarter of the blows a fighter throws in a match are pieces only he has; under a fifth, he gets more of his own or his weights change. gen_moveset.py --check reads it on the generated moves: mix is the part of a fighter's blows each cell throws, cells says which generated moves a cell draws on (as the recipes' pools do), and a piece is only his when it is his own and no other fighter of the roster has it. ownWeight: how many times likelier one of his own is drawn than another piece; 1 is the even draw of today's picker
gate._mix: measured on main 6581ede7: four seeded AI matches at medium, both fighters, 7,238 blows, the mean of the two. A player who holds, or who never mashes, throws another mix

pools._about: The pools of data/combat/recipes.json written from the cells (docs/combat/moveset-generator.md section 1: 'the seven pools, written by the generator from the cells, so Encounter's reader does not change'). tools/movegen/movegen.mjs writes them as pools.json, in the recipes file's own shape (a fighter to a pool to a list of {id, status}), and compares them with the live recipes in coverage.md. A pool row is a move whose key set plays as it is: levels names the keys' levels that do (a hand-state swap or a re-aim needs Animation's derivation first, so it waits). The id is the strike the move is posed on (keys.from), or for an energy piece the strike drawn for it (keys.strike); a strike that two moves share is one row. A rule: from, the cell; form, a form the move must have; filter, parts it must have; quota, the cell's quota whose filter it must meet; burst, the class of gap (parts.json strike.burst.classes) it must fit; also, a list in his identity row of move ids pinned into the pool whatever their form; neverAs, a weight at which his never rows are read too (the launcher's step lower plays a medium as a heavy)
